topics.title: Box Shadow, Text Shadow and Drop Shadow
topics.summary: Add depth with box-shadow, glow with text-shadow and shape-aware filter: drop-shadow().
topics.description:
### box-shadow
`box-shadow: offset-x offset-y blur spread color;` - only the two offsets are required.

```css
box-shadow: 0 4px 12px rgba(0,0,0,.15);      /* soft card */
box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 3px #4861ec;          /* inner ring */
box-shadow: 0 0 60px 20px #ffb000;            /* glow (spread 20px) */
box-shadow: 0 1px 2px #0003, 0 8px 24px #0002; /* layered, more realistic */
```

- **blur** softens, **spread** grows or shrinks the shadow.
- `inset` draws inside the box.
- Shadows follow `border-radius`, take **no layout space** and do not affect surrounding elements.
- Use `box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color` as a focus ring that is not clipped.

### text-shadow
`text-shadow: 2px 2px 5px rgba(0,0,0,.3);` - no spread or inset. Multiple comma-separated shadows give neon or outline effects.

### filter: drop-shadow()
Unlike box-shadow (rectangular), `drop-shadow()` follows the **alpha shape** of the element: transparent PNGs, SVGs, clip-path shapes and ::after triangles.

```css
img { filter: drop-shadow(5px 5px 15px rgba(0,0,0,.4)); }
```
No spread and no inset; the color can be before or after the lengths.

### When to use what
| Need | Use |
|---|---|
| Card elevation | box-shadow |
| Glow on text | text-shadow |
| Shadow of an icon/PNG/clipped shape | drop-shadow() |

### Performance
Large blurs are expensive when animated. Animate `opacity` of a pseudo-element holding the shadow instead of the shadow itself.

Layer several soft shadows for realism

Shadows do not take space in layout
pitfalls: Heavy blur radius animated on many elements (jank)
Using box-shadow on a transparent PNG and getting a square shadow
Shadow clipped by a parent with overflow: hidden

interview.q: Difference between box-shadow and filter: drop-shadow()?
interview.a: box-shadow follows the element's rectangular (rounded) box. drop-shadow follows the actual rendered alpha shape, so it works with transparent images and clipped shapes.

interview.q: What do the values in box-shadow mean?
interview.a: offset-x, offset-y, blur radius, spread radius, color; plus the optional inset keyword.

interview.q: How do you create an inner shadow?
interview.a: Add the inset keyword: box-shadow: inset 0 0 10px #000.

topics.title: Filters and backdrop-filter
topics.summary: Blur, brighten, grayscale and color-shift elements, or the area behind them.
topics.description:
`filter` applies graphical effects to an element and its content. Effects can be chained with spaces.

| Function | Example | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `blur()` | `blur(5px)` | gaussian blur |
| `brightness()` | `brightness(1.5)` | lighter/darker |
| `contrast()` | `contrast(0.8)` | |
| `grayscale()` | `grayscale(1)` | black and white |
| `sepia()` | `sepia(.7)` | warm vintage tone |
| `saturate()` | `saturate(2)` | color intensity |
| `hue-rotate()` | `hue-rotate(90deg)` | shifts hues |
| `invert()` | `invert(1)` | negative |
| `opacity()` | `opacity(.5)` | |
| `drop-shadow()` | see shadows | |

```css
img { filter: blur(3px) grayscale(.5) contrast(1.2); }   /* from the source demo */
img:hover { filter: none; transition: filter .3s; }
```

### backdrop-filter
Applies the same functions to **what is behind** the element - the basis of frosted-glass UIs.

```css
.glass { background: rgba(255,255,255,.2); backdrop-filter: blur(10px) saturate(150%); }
```
The element must be at least partially transparent for the effect to be visible. Safari needs the `-webkit-` prefix on older versions.

### Tips
- Filters create a new stacking context and containing block for fixed children.
- Animate filter values for smooth hover states (grayscale -> color).
- Heavy blurs on large areas cost GPU time; keep them small or limited to a few elements.
- `filter: blur()` on a parent blurs its text too; use `backdrop-filter` for background-only blur.
keyPoints: Chain several filter functions separated by spaces
grayscale, blur, brightness, contrast, hue-rotate are most useful
backdrop-filter filters what is behind the element
filter creates a new stacking context
Animate filters for polished hover effects
pitfalls: Using filter: blur on a container when only the background should blur
No transparency, so backdrop-filter shows nothing
Too many large blurred layers hurting scrolling performance

interview.q: How do you combine multiple filters?
interview.a: List them in one filter declaration separated by spaces, e.g. filter: blur(3px) grayscale(.5) contrast(1.2).

interview.q: What is the difference between filter: blur and backdrop-filter: blur?
interview.a: filter blurs the element itself and its content; backdrop-filter blurs whatever is rendered behind the element.

interview.q: Why does my backdrop-filter show nothing?
interview.a: The element's background is fully opaque or there is no content behind it; use a semi-transparent background.

topics.title: Blend Modes: mix-blend-mode and background-blend-mode
topics.summary: Blend overlapping elements or background layers like Photoshop layers.
topics.description:
**Blend modes** control how colors of overlapping layers combine, like layer modes in Photoshop.

### Two properties
| Property | Blends |
|---|---|
| `mix-blend-mode` | the element with whatever is **behind** it |
| `background-blend-mode` | the element's own **background layers** (image + color/gradient) |
| `isolation: isolate` | stops an element's blending from reaching below its group |

### Common modes
- `multiply` - darkens; white disappears (great for shadows and tinting).
- `screen` - lightens; black disappears.
- `overlay`, `soft-light`, `hard-light` - increase contrast.
- `difference`, `exclusion` - inverted-looking effects, good for cursors.
- `darken`, `lighten`, `color-dodge`, `color-burn`, `hue`, `saturation`, `color`, `luminosity`.

### Examples
```css
.hero {
  background-color: #ff3368;
  background-image: url(photo.jpg);
  background-blend-mode: multiply;   /* tinted photo */
}
.title { mix-blend-mode: difference; color: white; } /* text inverts over any background */
```

### Practical uses
- Duotone / tinted hero images with no image editing.
- Text that stays readable over mixed backgrounds (difference).
- Custom cursors and neon overlays (screen / lighten).
- Subtle texture overlays with `multiply` or `soft-light`.

### Notes
- Blend modes create stacking contexts and can affect performance on large layers.
- Always check contrast manually - blending changes colors dynamically.
keyPoints: mix-blend-mode blends an element with what is behind it
background-blend-mode blends background layers of the same element
multiply darkens, screen lightens, difference inverts
Use isolation: isolate to limit blending scope
Great for tinted images and adaptive text
pitfalls: Applying mix-blend-mode when the backdrop is transparent (no visible effect)
Unexpected blending with page elements beyond the component (use isolation)
Relying on blending for essential text without contrast checks

It multiplies the color values, so the result is darker; white stays unchanged and black stays black.

interview.q: How do you limit blending to a component?
interview.a: Add isolation: isolate on its container so the blend does not reach elements outside.

topics.title: clip-path and Shapes
topics.summary: Cut elements into circles, polygons and custom shapes with clip-path.
topics.description:
`clip-path` defines the visible region of an element. Everything outside the shape is hidden (and not clickable).

### Shape functions
| Function | Example |
|---|---|
| `circle()` | `circle(50% at 50% 50%)` |
| `ellipse()` | `ellipse(50% 30% at 50% 50%)` |
| `inset()` | `inset(10px 20px round 12px)` |
| `polygon()` | `polygon(50% 0, 100% 100%, 0 100%)` triangle |
| `path()` | SVG path string |

### Polygon examples (from the source course)
```css
/* octagon */
clip-path: polygon(20% 0, 80% 0, 100% 20%, 100% 80%, 80% 100%, 20% 100%, 0 80%, 0 20%);
/* arrow */
clip-path: polygon(40% 0, 40% 20%, 100% 20%, 100% 80%, 40% 80%, 40% 100%, 0 50%);
/* circle */
clip-path: circle();
```

### Why use it
- Hero sections with angled edges.
- Image masks, badges, speech bubbles, arrows, stars.
- **Animation**: transition between two polygons with the **same number of points**.
- Reveal effects: animate `clip-path: inset(0 100% 0 0)` to `inset(0)`.

### Notes
- The clipped area also clips shadows; use `filter: drop-shadow()` on a parent wrapper to add a shadow.
- Use online generators (like Clippy) to draw polygon points visually.
- `shape-outside` is the sibling property for wrapping text around a shape.

circle(), ellipse(), inset(), polygon(), path()
Percentages make shapes responsive
Animate between shapes with equal point counts
Shadows get clipped - use drop-shadow on a wrapper

Interpolating polygons with different numbers of points (no animation)

interview.q: Why does my box-shadow disappear with clip-path?
interview.a: The shadow is outside the clipped region and gets cut. Wrap the element and apply filter: drop-shadow() on the wrapper.
Yes, between shapes of the same type and point count (e.g., two polygons with equal vertices).

topics.title: Glassmorphism and Neumorphism Recipes
topics.summary: Two popular UI styles built from transparency, blur and layered shadows.
topics.description:
These are visual **styles**, built from properties you already know.

### Glassmorphism
A frosted-glass card floating over a colorful background.

Ingredients:
1. A vivid/gradient background behind the card.
2. Semi-transparent background: `rgba(255,255,255,.15)`.
3. `backdrop-filter: blur(12px) saturate(150%)`.
4. A thin light border: `1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.3)`.
5. Soft shadow: `0 8px 32px rgba(0,0,0,.2)`.

### Neumorphism (soft UI)
Elements look extruded from the same-colored surface using **two opposite shadows**: a light one top-left and a dark one bottom-right.

```css
.neu {
  background: #e0e5ec;
  border-radius: 20px;
  box-shadow: 9px 9px 16px #a3b1c6, -9px -9px 16px #ffffff;
}
.neu:active { box-shadow: inset 6px 6px 10px #a3b1c6, inset -6px -6px 10px #fff; }
```

### Cautions (accessibility)
- Glass: ensure text contrast against the *worst* area of the background; add a darker tint if needed.
- Neumorphism: low contrast between element and background - boundaries are hard to see for low-vision users. Use it for decoration, and add clear borders or icons for important controls.
- Provide `@supports (backdrop-filter: blur(1px))` fallback with a more opaque background.

### Tips
- Keep blur values moderate (8-16px) for performance.
- Use CSS variables so one palette generates both light and dark shadows.
keyPoints: Glass = translucent background + backdrop-filter blur + light border
Neumorphism = same-color surface + light and dark opposite shadows
Pressed state uses inset shadows
Check contrast and provide fallbacks
Keep blur moderate for performance
pitfalls: Glass card over a plain white background (effect invisible)
No fallback when backdrop-filter is unsupported

interview.q: How is neumorphism created in CSS?
interview.a: With a background equal to the page surface and two box-shadows: one light (negative offset) and one dark (positive offset); inset shadows for pressed state.

interview.q: What is the main downside of neumorphism?
interview.a: Low contrast makes boundaries and states hard to perceive, which hurts accessibility.
